notes: Identity assessment: supplied file is a frozen collection of web-parser excerpts of a manuscript mirror, not a complete canonical article or PDF. Its displayed title is truncated to “Replicating the effects of a teacher-scaffolded”; the provenance header claims title verification against Harvard, but that claim cannot be independently checked within the allowed material. The excerpt contains first-person Methods, Results, Discussion and primary tables for READS, 19 North Carolina schools, spring/fall 2011 third graders, replication of Kim and White (2008), and poverty moderation, consistent with the neutral replication reference. Author byline, full title, DOI and bibliographic year are not visible in these excerpts, so full bibliographic identity remains provisional. This appears to be primary manuscript content rather than a secondary summary or preregistration. No PDF was supplied. Manuscript pagination differs from the supplied p. 18 locator; manuscript p. 18 concerns background, not the outcome test. Target ambiguity: the generic intervention/ITBS description does not distinguish the basic teacher-lessons/summer-books arm (TL-SB) from the enhanced arm with teacher calls (TL-SB-TC), pooled lesson routines from the exact multiple-strategy/fluency replication subset, or poverty-specific effects. The source explicitly designates basic TL-SB as its replication question, which makes it a strong candidate but does not establish that the assigned row selects it. Table 4 Model 1 prints TL-SB = -0.043 (SE 0.050) and TL-SB-TC = -0.017 (SE 0.050), N = 1189. These are coefficients on standardized pretest/posttest outcomes: p. 31 explicitly calls them standardized covariate-adjusted posttest differences; do not label them unstandardized b or convert them. Prose rounds these to - .04 and - .02 and states no difference; neither Model 1 treatment coefficient has a significance symbol, and the inspected text does not supply its exact numeric p or an explicit same-test p bound. Do not substitute the poverty-interaction p = .06 or .03. Candidate model N = 1189 students (not schools): explicit Model 1 N, consistent with posttest N = 1,189 after 16% attrition from 1,421. No N is derived from df or summed here. Table 3 all-school group counts 396, 395, 397 total 1188 and therefore are not silently substituted for the explicitly printed model N. Retain the common model N only as a candidate for parent field-scope review while coefficient correspondence is unresolved. Reported success records the explicit full-sample nonreplication verdict; the authors also describe positive high-poverty-school effects. Original side is unassigned and is a placeholder, not an assessment of original-source availability.
